caption:
New car. Closing in danger?

A mortgage approval is not always the finish line. Before closing in Mississauga, ask these questions: 1) Your lender may re-check your credit and your job before closing, so ask your lender or mortgage broker what they check. 2) A new car loan or credit card before closing may change your approval, so ask before you borrow. 3) Keep records showing where your down payment came from, because your lawyer and lender may ask. 4) Thinking of changing jobs before closing? Talk to your lender first. These are planning questions, not rules: your lender and your agreement of purchase and sale decide the details.

Bought first. Old home unsold?

Picture this: you found your next home in Georgetown, but your current home has not sold yet. Questions to ask before you buy first: 1) Buying before you sell can mean carrying the costs of two homes for a while. 2) Ask your lender whether bridge financing is an option, and what it costs. 3) Adding a condition to sell first may make your offer less attractive, so ask your Realtor® how that could play out. 4) Ask your lawyer about lining up both closing dates. These are planning questions, not promises: your lender, your lawyer and your agreements decide the details, and no sale price or timeline is guaranteed.

$10K bonus. Interest saved?

Example only: a $500,000 mortgage in Brampton, 25-year amortization, 4.34% fixed (interest compounded semi-annually, same rate for the whole amortization).
1) Monthly mortgage: $2,723.07.
2) After 12 payments the balance is about $488,607. A $10,000 prepayment brings it to $478,607.
3) Keeping the same monthly mortgage, total interest drops from $316,920 to $299,352, which is $17,568 less, and the mortgage is paid off about 10 months sooner (290 payments instead of 300).
Prepayment privileges, limits and penalties differ by lender and mortgage, so check yours first. 4.34% is an example from the lowest advertised 5-year fixed rates (insured); uninsured rates can differ, and rates change at renewal. Lenders also apply the stress test and debt ratios.

caption:
Caledon home. Is the water safe?

Buying a rural home in Caledon? Questions to ask before you go firm: 1) Does the home have a well and septic system, or town water and sewer? 2) Ask for recent well water test results, and consider getting your own test. 3) Ask for the septic records, like pumping, repairs and past inspections. 4) Ask your inspector, or a specialist, to check the well and septic system. These are planning questions, not rules: ask your lawyer and your Realtor® how to build them into your offer.
